source_priority: FAQ corrections; RR over LTP; printed effects read subject to those texts. Module supplies only original-image locations.

adjudications.verdict: normal printed effect available; exact priority and impossible-cost edge not explicitly adjudicated

controlling_text.text: Place 1 prisec unit in any district to remove all other units in that district.
When a prisec unit is placed in a district containing an enemy unit, that enemy unit must move.
When a component must be placed, if there are none of that type remaining in the reserve, do not place that component.
The explicit card-over-reference priority bullet is for an asset card ability; it does not expressly establish a universal action-card placement/cost timing rule.

adjudications.resolved: Arrest Orders specifically instructs removal of all other units, not tokens. Riot Control sacrifices a prisec to remove up to two enemies; Scorched Earth requires outage placement in a district not in outage and removes enemies in that district and one other same-tier district. RR10 settles component nonplacement at empty reserve.
adjudications.precise_unresolved_issue: For Arrest Orders with an enemy present and available prisec, the ordinary placement meets the RR enemy-must-move trigger while the card explicitly says placement to remove. Assigned sources do not expressly identify a checkpoint/priority that says whether removal prevents that movement or whether the movement can occur before the removal instruction. Separately, RR10 does not state whether failure to place a required component cancels a following to-remove effect. Do not conflate the ordinary priority tension with the impossible-cost edge.
adjudications.signoff_limit: An unqualified claim that every ordinary Arrest Orders outcome is authoritatively adjudicated is blocked. The exact printed-instruction question Q60 is supported and can remain; do not grade a newly invented universal cost/priority conclusion. A report explicitly disclosing this narrow limit may otherwise present the supported core procedures.
adjudications.resolution_needed: An explicit controlling interpretation of the action-specific placement/removal relationship or official clarification; a fan script or generic stack assumption cannot supply it.

adjudications.verdict: specific routine setup/demand instructions support facedown top return

controlling_text.text: Each player draws two investment cards ... returns the remaining card facedown to the top of the investment deck.
All investment cards are returned to the investment deck, and the deck is shuffled. Then ... remaining investment cards are returned facedown to the top of the investment deck.
Discarded investment cards are shuffled into the investment deck without being revealed.
All of the investment cards are shuffled together to reform the deck ... returns the unchosen card facedown to the top of the investment deck.

adjudications.resolved: Follow the explicit sequence for ordinary full setup and demand: top-return of unchosen cards facedown. At later Choose Investment, first return all investments and shuffle, then draw/choose/top-return. Distinguish that explicit return from the generic discarded-card wording of RR33.2; do not insert an extra shuffle after each unchosen return.
adjudications.precise_unresolved_issue: RR33 intro loosely calls the unchosen card discarded, so same-document terminology is inconsistent. No FAQ erratum changes this. The detailed routine procedures agree with LTP and give a usable exact instruction; this is a disclosed interpretation of inconsistent wording, not an invented official erratum.
adjudications.candidate_answer_assessment: Q01/Q15 expected top-return treatment is supported. Preserve source-conflict note; no correction to those expected outcomes required.

adjudications.verdict: cancellation facts controlled; exposed-card/status interpretation has a narrow ambiguity

controlling_text.text: When a new counteroffer is proposed, the previous counteroffer is no longer the counteroffer and the previous countering player is no longer the countering player.
Only the topmost card in the Counteroffer box is the counteroffer. Previous counteroffers are ignored except for determining how many cards a player must discard to propose a new counteroffer.
Chief Gorman ... can return a counteroffer ... That player ceases to be the countering player and does not return ... cards ... discarded ... to propose the counteroffer.
After a counteroffer is proposed, you may exhaust this card to return the counteroffer to the countering player’s hand unless he gives you 2 capital. He cannot propose another counteroffer this turn.

adjudications.resolved: Return the cancelled current offer, remove that proposer’s countering status, do not refund proposal discards, and do not let that proposer propose again. RR15.5 remains the controlling topmost-card rule, not permission to choose any earlier card or resurrect a card that has left the box.
adjudications.precise_unresolved_issue: If an older card is exposed after the top offer returns, the positive topmost rule strongly supports treating that now-top card as the counteroffer. The text also says superseded cards/players cease those statuses and provides no express sentence restoring the earlier proposer after Chief. The supplied corpus does not separately explain that status restoration. This is a narrow reading issue in one named interaction, not evidence for a general interrupt/stack framework.
adjudications.signoff_limit: Q31 asks cancellation/status/no-refund facts, and its expected answer stays within explicit text. Ordinary supported core signoff can disclose this narrow status issue. Do not claim a separately verified exhaustive revival ruling or a categorical no-revival rule. If such a branch is demanded for an unqualified all-interactions signoff, retain it as unresolved.
adjudications.resolution_needed: Official explanation of now-exposed prior counteroffer/proposer status, or a clearly stated interpretation based on RR15.5, distinguished from an express printed ruling.

ordinary_signoff_conclusion: SG02 does not block; SG03 permits supported Q31 with stated limit. SG01 has an ordinary-card priority issue as well as a separate impossible-cost edge, so an unconditional fully adjudicated complete-core claim must remain qualified.
